text:
Rosalind Tavner founded the Quillfeather Archive in 2009, according to a deed filed this week with the Veyland Registry. The disclosure puts a name to the long-rumoured origin of the private records house, which now holds more than 4.2 million indexed documents and generated 18.6 million crowns in licensing revenue last year.

Tavner, now 61, launched the archive after leaving Sable & Morrow, where she ran document recovery. Early backing came from two family trusts and a 3.4 million-crown bridge loan from Northgate Mercantile.

For the records-management sector, the filing matters because ownership clarity can ease consolidation talks. Analysts at Bracken Roe say independent archives with clean provenance are likely to command higher valuations as compliance demand rises.
